quotes.excerpt: Queen in Black Issue 2 brings everything to the party. Cosmic Marvel is combining with the Earth in brutal fashion. They have been separated for a long time, and Asgard is locked down. But this event brings it crashing down. You can tell from every piece of dialogue and every illustrated line that there’s a love of superhero comics and every corner of the weird and wonderful universe.

Event fatigue is running wild at Marvel but ‘Queen In Black’ might have the juice to beat it as the debut issue proves. Character continuity is a bit messy, but the overall story and visuals are on point and are actually a bit exciting to engage with.

The Smart Division #2 will inject a level of fear into the reader that they may not have thought an issue could do. This may be a story, but, Zack, John, and Hassan blur the lines of reality, posing ethical questions regarding AI and leaving us with an ending that sinks us deeper into the mystery.

The Smart Division #2 builds confidently on the series’ opening mystery with sharper tension, compelling character conflict, and an unsettling exploration of AI and corporate power. Zack Kaplan keeps the investigation unpredictable, while John J. Pearson delivers immersive artwork that strengthens the book’s noir atmosphere. This is a smart, suspenseful second issue that leaves the case more dangerous and more intriguing than ever. If this series isn’t already on your Pull List, reconsider that decision NOW.

Hammer Head is one of those comics that I knew would be worth reading, but surprised the hell out of me in such a fantastic way. Writer Ed Brisson and illustrator Damian Couceiro craft a gloriously twisted must-read horror that delivers all the bloody fun of a classic slasher while carving out something uniquely its own.

Hammer Head #1 is a gripping debut that blends emotional character work with slow-building horror. Ed Brisson’s tense storytelling and the art team’s bleak, atmospheric visuals make Jules’ nightmare immediately compelling while leaving enough unanswered questions to demand the reader pick up issue two. Horror fans should add this promising new series to their Pull List immediately.

Hammerfist #2 is how you ratchet up the ridiculousness set by its first issue without sacrificing quality character and story work. There’s so much more carnage to be had, and I do not doubt that this team will deliver.

Hammerfist #2 is a non-stop, raucous sprint through a little desert town that never lets up. Rick Remender’s grindhouse spectacular kicks things into another gear as Mike Denton’s world has been turned completely upside down. Steve Epting’s art and Matt Hollingsworth’s colors provide the perfect palette this violent story demands. This is one of my favorite series of the year.

Erica’s return to present time brings forth a much needed encounter behind heavy drama. Tynion IV opens deep wounds with incredible writing. Dell’edera and Muerto craft the intense exchanges with superb art. No one does slow burn drama better than SIKTC!

The things that Haun and his team are doing are truly electric and terrifying. “Dooney Hollow” is for those that love slow burn horror with plenty of mystery and fall vibes. If you want that, then you need to pick this up!

The Folk of Dooney Hollow #1 is a compelling horror debut that pairs a steadily unfolding mystery with atmospheric artwork and an unsettling Ozark setting. Its strong pacing, memorable final reveal, and lingering unanswered questions make the next issue an easy recommendation. Make sure to pick a copy of this first issue up when you are at the shop this week. Also, well you are there, you should just add this to your Pull List as I’m confident that you will want more of this amazing and eerie world.

Conan the Barbarian #35 is another winning issue in a winning arc. Jim Zub’s tale of Conan and his allies confronting a cosmic horror ranks up there with the best of Robert E. Howard’s stories, and the art is a gorgeous fit for the material.
Black Tower: The Raven Conspiracy #1 is a compelling mix of magic and spy fiction, packed with haunting imagery and a unique mystery.

Black Tower: The Raven Conspiracy #1 proves that everything out of DC Vertigo should be jumped on immediately. This was a strong start to a comic series that has captured my attention from the first page and didn’t let go until the ending. I cannot recommend this comic enough!
G.I. Joe #25 is a major milestone done right, paying off years of buildup and kicking off the series' most epic storyline yet.

G.I. JOE #25 is a phenomenal start to the Nightforce story arc. Joshua Williamson, Tom Reilly and Andrea Milana pace things out that you feel like you are experiencing the start of a big blockbuster event. Everything that happens in this issue comes across as being a payoff for many sub-plots that have been developed since the start of the series. Where the payoff leads to is anyone’s guess, leaving you as the reader even more excited to find out what happens next.

Superman #40 is damn near perfect. This arc acted as a bit of a redemption for Superboy Prime and I absolutely adore him after this. Whilst the story here is wrapped up, this isn’t the last time we will see Superboy Prime and there seems to be a bright future ahead for him and his “supporting characters”.

This has been a phenomenal story setting up Prime’s future, but special credit once again goes to Dan Mora, who plays with the nature of the comic book format in some incredibly unique ways. The original Superman is back next month for the kickoff of the big “Kingdom of Zod” event, but I hope Williamson gets to keep writing Prime for a long time.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #300 (#20) not only pushes the great story that we have been following forward, but also gives this milestone issue a big feel as well. The drama, action, surprises, and emotions are firing on all cylinders in this issue. If this issue doesn’t make you feel something you may need to check your pulse. They could’ve just phoned this one in as the 300th issue milestone is more than enough to sell the book. But they didn’t phone it in at all and crafted an issue that is sure to bring readers back next month for issue 21. If Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is not on your Pull List already it needs to be added ASAP! If you are a comic book collector this 300th issue needs to be added to your collection as well. Cheers to 300 issues of TMNT and can’t wait for the 400th milestone issue!

This issue takes you on an emotional ride! Sure there is plenty of action within these pages. All while tugging at your heart strings with the current situation revolving around Shen. Losing a loved one and having the chance to bring them back is going to hit home with many readers I suspect. You do not want to miss out on this start of a new storyline for this series of TMNT. Go get your copy today!

Operation: Iron Coffin #3 delivers a thrilling, blood-soaked finale that balances outrageous action with genuine emotional weight. Kenny Porter brings Dracula’s conflict with his children to a satisfying close, while Tyrell Cannon and Shawn Lee give the issue relentless visual energy. Brutal, heartfelt, and wildly entertaining, this is a fitting conclusion to the series. This has been one of my favorite series of the year and is one of the most entertaining series on the shelves. If for whatever reason you missed this one, try and get the issues at your LCS this week. If you can’t find them, definitely pick up the trade when it drops, so you don’t miss out on one of the best series of the year!

“Operation: Iron Coffin” is an absolute tour de force from start to finish. If you ever feel down about yourself, read this to remind yourself you’re so much more. If someone or something like Dracula can redeem himself, then so can we.

Operation: Iron Coffin #2 keeps the momentum going with a bigger, bloodier, and more personal chapter for Dracula. Kenny Porter deepens the story without slowing down the action, while Tyrell Cannon’s artwork delivers the chaos, horror, and energy this concept demands. This series continues to be an absolute blast and remains an easy Pull List recommendation. Do not sleep on this series! Make sure you jump on this train now, as you don’t want to miss what happens next.

I don’t know how they’re doing it, but “Operation: Iron Coffin” is one of the best out this year. Kenny Porter manages to create a version of Dracula that feels relatable yet horrifying. His writing coupled with Cannon’s fantastic artwork create a truly amazing reading experience.
It’s pure joy when a great story is united with unique artwork. And that’s what this miniseries is delivering so far. It’s not just a great fantasy series, it’s just a great comic series. Period.

In the world of contemporary sword and sorcery fantasy, it takes a hell of a lot of guts to deliver a story so completely devoid of any kind of humor that is also relentlessly dark. It runs the risk of being a parody of itself. However, the entire creative team does such a good job of delivering the proper intensity. It feels pure. It feels dark. And it feels like a perfect realization of a very classic and classic dark sort of epic heroes journey. It's not something that's attempted as much in the modern age as one might think. Contemporary fantasy has a tendency to be very self-conscious and wait itself very carefully on the page. Krman Blade is heroically, unflinchingly dark.
One of the best series in comics right now. The art is wild, creative, adventurous, and stunning. The story keeps drawing you back in issue after issue.
Marc Spector: Moon Knight #7 delivers an exhilarating ride with huge action, incredible artwork, and deadly stakes. It leaves you itching for the next issue.

The Smart Division is a fantastic science-fiction mystery that eerily could be more fact than fiction. Writer Zack Kaplan delivers a timely detective tale exploring the use of modern technology in solving crimes. However, it’s the juxtaposition of John Pearson’s elegant brush strokes that makes story rise above the rest. Kaplan and Pearson’s creativity knows no bounds and The Smart Division is proof of that.

I sat down with The Smart Division expecting a slick sci-fi detective story and walked away rattled about the world outside my window. That is the highest thing I can say about a comic right now. This is a perfect debut and one of the most relevant books on the stands, and I cannot wait to see where the case goes.

King Shazam and Superman throw down in a final fight for the ages! Arron leaves it all on table with the script. The art team never knows a ceiling in how far to raise the stakes. Highest possible recommendation.

Absolute Superman #21 feels like a true spectacle and lives up to the hype in every way as this arc comes to. a close. There is so much violence, emotion, and power packed into these pages that it may, in fact, be my favorite issue of the run yet.
Superman: The Stranger #1 returns to Clark Kent's roots, spinning a story that shows why Superman is such a timeless character.

The best Superman comic I’ve read in years!  A 1930s reinvention of the Man of Steel that returns Superman to his 1930s roots, but zigs and zags in ways you won’t expect, while keeping you on your toes. With a story that hooks you from the go and art and colours that leap off the page, this is a must-read mini-series.

Six of Us #1 turns a seemingly perfect 1990s sitcom cast into a web of secrets, resentment, and murder, with Tom King and Gabriel Hernández Walta delivering a compelling mystery that leaves everyone looking potentially guilty.

SIX OF US reminds us why this award winning creative team is so unstoppable. It's a human story about the importance of creating art, but the cost of it too. Six of Us #1 invites us to consider what true fulfillment looks like, and whether it has anything to do with success.
Black Tower: The Raven Conspiracy #1 is a compelling mix of magic and spy fiction, packed with haunting imagery and a unique mystery.

Black Tower: The Raven Conspiracy #1 proves that everything out of DC Vertigo should be jumped on immediately. This was a strong start to a comic series that has captured my attention from the first page and didn’t let go until the ending. I cannot recommend this comic enough!

While some may balk at having to buy another book for the complete story again, the strong character work and action of Detective Comics #1114 should convince even the stingiest of comic book fans that it was worth the price of admission

Batman forms an uneasy alliance with the Freezes to save Gotham in this “Bad Seeds” tie-in! Taylor adds a few layers into the dangerous trek for hope. Henry and Estouco deliver on huge moments while keeping events very grounded between an unhappy couple. A great lead-in for where “Bad Seeds” is going to finish.

Damian Wayne gives Nightwing a helping hand but is it already too late for Gotham? Watters lets the pair loose while spotlighting the toll taken on Grayson. Lapham and the art team present a stacked vision of events with some bonding moments thrown in the mix. Putting the karma out there: Watters could write an excellent “Nightwing and Robin” series.
Nightwing #143 is jam-packed with Nightwing and Robin doing what they do best: fighting crime together!

Ra’s Al Ghul keeps the world on the edge of destruction while the Finest scramble to defend! Waid orchestrates events to a magnificant level with the writing. Gutiérrez & the team go for incredible swings with the art. An impressive read from start to close.

Batman / Superman: World's Finest #56 keeps its event-sized storyline moving with exciting Superman action and an intriguing look at Ra's al Ghul's environmental motivations. Mark Waid makes the villain's perspective surprisingly compelling, while Batman's role as a strategist reinforces the crisis's scale. Adrian Gutierrez and Luis Guerrero deliver energetic visuals, particularly during Superman's explosive confrontations. A redundant exchange with a villain briefly stalls the momentum, but the issue remains an entertaining chapter with plenty at stake.
Catwoman #92 continues to counter the high-stakes Bad Seeds crossover with emotional weight.

Wonder Woman #38 pushes the Matriarch's plans closer to fruition, delivering impressive action as Tom King and Daniel Sampere prepare for the run's conclusion. Nubia gets a particularly strong showing, with Sampere's dynamic artwork making her confrontation with the Matriarch a highlight. Unfortunately, the story relies too heavily on questionable character decisions to advance the villain's plans, leaving Diana sidelined and the stakes feeling somewhat manufactured. The cliffhanger promises a massive superhero showdown, but the path there feels a little too convenient.

Wonder Woman #38 does a great job showing the huge contrast between Wonder Woman and The Matriarch with their differing personalities and how far they’re willing to go to do what they feel is morally right.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #23 delivers a tense, emotionally grounded issue that blends supernatural horror, fast-paced action, and striking artwork. With General Eight Thunders’ threat growing and the boundary between life and death collapsing, the issue leaves the Turtles facing their most personal battle yet and builds strong anticipation for what will come next. If you haven’t been reading this TMNT run, you are truly missing out.

New Titans gets better and better and that’s made clear in New Titans #40. This issue was intense, it was drenched in heightened emotions, and it kept your eyes glued to the pages. Excellent job by the creative team!

The Titans find themselves in over their head as Commodore Murphy manipulates matters in his favor. Brombal lets Eva and Static get some much needed time to impress. The art team lets loose on great action and mounting drama. After a more confusing start, it looks like this team is finally starting to come together.
This wasn’t the flashiest installment of the series, but it’s one that was absolutely essential to Simon’s emotional recovery from his most heartfelt tragedy.

Redcoat #21 shows Simon Pure at his lowest yet. How does a man who cannot die move forward in life without the ones that he loves? The team brings so much emotion out of the panels, delivering hints of beauty and hope amongst the tragedy. Albert and Simon’s relationship continues to grow and is one of beauty as well, making this issue take us for a ride emotionally.
GI Joe 27 keeps the fun rolling in one of comic’s best reads. The Joes and Night Force are getting on the same page, but it might be too late to stop Zartan from getting a major win.
G.I. Joe #27 delivers powerful tension, blending high-stakes team infighting, Zartan's deceptive maneuvering, and gorgeous art into a gripping narrative that rewards long-time readers.

Superman Unlimited #18 kicks off a bold new path for Jon Kent, and a new creative direction for the book. It's a fresh start that's more than welcome, especially since it puts some big ideas on the table.

It’s a new day for Jon Kent but not everyone is ready for it! Slott puts the bond between father and son to the test with the script. Meyer and Peratelli’s art orchestrates the deep conversations while reflecting on the past. A new day has arrived & Jon Kent may never be the same again!

Marshall makes his move but is it too late? That is the question haunting the road to Radiant Black #50. The writing balances out a reunion while attempting a daring rescue. Impressive images capture the moments to elevate the drama higher. Radiant Black continues to be the blueprint for modern superhero storytelling !
Radiant Black #44 kicks off a new story arc while testing the relationship at the core of the series. It also reminds us that the future isn't set in stone, whether you're a hero or a villain.

The Nice House by the Sea #12 delivers a riveting conclusion that puts Norah firmly in the driver's seat as two worlds hurtle toward destruction. James Tynion IV crafts a surprisingly accessible finale built around a tense series of conversations, while Álvaro Martínez Bueno and Jordie Bellaire make the impending apocalypse look breathtaking. The final pages focus more on setting up the next chapter than on providing complete closure, but there's no denying how effectively this issue brings its immediate conflict to a close.

One resident of the Houses attempts the unthinkable as the end of the world has arrived!! Tynion cuts deeply into the soul of the series with phenomenal writing. Bueno and Bellaire electrify as the art sweeps readers under its spell. An impressive journey into the soul of humanity.

reason.snippet: Jeff the Land Shark: Superstar #4 is a fun issue for any avid TV and movie watcher. Kelly Thompson really leans into some classic TV and movie tropes while Tokitokoro and Jim Campbell’s anime-style art complements the TV feel of this issue.
pros: Thompson adapts classic TV and movie tropes into a comics in a fun and engaging way.
Tokitokoro and Jim Campbell’s artwork compliements the TV feel of this issue.
Tokitokoro and Campbell’s artwork is very dynamic and expressive even outside of the typical anime style.
cons: The Mojo and M.O.D.O.K. storyline feels like it'll be rushed since it was introduced so close to the end of the miniseries.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Absolute Green Arrow #6 delivers a satisfying conclusion to its central mystery, with a reveal that makes sense for the characters and the Absolute Universe. Dinah gets some of the issue's best moments, especially as the story lays the groundwork for something much bigger. The lengthy stretches of exposition occasionally make the issue feel more concerned with explaining itself than letting events…
pros: The second Green Arrow reveal is clever, satisfying, and well explained.
Dinah's quick thinking and surprising new direction are highlights.
A strong cliffhanger raises the stakes considerably.
cons: Several pages of exposition slow the story's momentum.
The epilogue relies too heavily on explanation to establish the next arc.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Batwoman #8 is a fun team up for Batwoman and Huntress, two badass characters who may not always see eye-to-eye, but manage to settle their differences long enough to unite around a common cause.
pros: Epic team up of Batwoman and Huntress made for some great dialogue exchanges between the two characters, as well as some awesome action sequences.
The scene of Kate explaining why the TUCOs are not soldiers is a great distillation of the morals and values that guide Kate Kane, not only as a crime fighter,…

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Nightwing #143 is jam-packed with Nightwing and Robin doing what they do best: fighting crime together!
pros: Nightwing and Robin's team-up continues to be a blast to see unfold
Dan Watters continues to take the seeds planted during 'Dark Patterns' by bringing another familiar face back into the fray
The tie-in to the recent Batgirl issue was the most perfect example of how comics can overlap without being a clustered mess

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: With a measured pace, Vampirella #7 explores ideas of mercy, forgiveness, and atonement as characters new and old interact in intriguing ways.
pros: Christopher Priest gives the issue a strong thematic through line.
Davis Goetten's artwork is fantastic, delivering tons of character.
Giovanni Caputo creates some intriguing sequences through a more subdued palette.
cons: The return of Benny may leave some newer readers feeling a bit lost.
Some readers may be put off by the series' pacing.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: This first issue kicks off the miniseries with a plethora of intriguing characters and has a beautifully Grand Guignol-style climax that will thrill any horror fan.
pros: Writer Pallie Paul Allor imbues the characters with a great variety of personalities and the snippy dialog is hilarious at times.
Artist Chris Evenhuis and colorist Sjan Weijers deliver beautiful art throughout the book. I especially love Eliza's icy blue eyes.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Though it starts off strong, X-Men United #8 loses its momentum in the end, letting the conflict resolve a little too abruptly in order to set up the next chapter of the series. What is nice though, is that it feels like this series has found an identity that works. The strongest issues of X-Men United have seen the X-Men team up with non-mutant heroes, something that will hopefully continue as th…
pros: It's always nice to see Dani Moonstar, Blade, and Bloodline get love.
Eve L. Ewing and Evan Narcisse do a good job avoiding some tired tropes.
Tiago Palma's action sequences are visually dynamic.
cons: The climax of the issue falls short, focusing a little too strongly on setting up the next chapter rather than providing a satisfying conclusion.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Coastal Chaos #2 balances laughs and tension well and gives Armaggon enough personality to be more than a gimmick. If you liked the first issue, this one delivers more of what worked and makes the series feel bigger. It’s a fun, good-looking comic that treats its young audience and its longtime TMNT fans with respect.
pros: Armaggon is a standout: great design with real motivation.
Great moments from supporting cast.
Joyce's color palatte really adds to the atmoshpere of the creature feature.
cons: Armaggon’s backstory is teased but left unanswered.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: New Titans #40 makes up for an avalanche of plot points with visually gripping artwork and some great character moments, but it's pretty clear that the Titans need to get over their issues and work as a team. Early books showed this series has plenty of potential, and I hope it fully taps into it.
pros: Basri's artwork brings focus to certain elements, particularly Wonder Girl.
Lucas' use of color makes sure that each member of the Titans stands out.
cons: A lot of plot points are fighting for attention in Brombal's script.
When will the Titans stop fighting each other and work as a team?

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Spider-Man: Miles Morales #3 finally reveals the secret origin of its new villain, while forever shaking up the young web-slinger's world. One thing's for certain: Miles's life will never be the same, and how he deals with it will shape his place in the Marvel Universe.
pros: Hill finally reveals Revenant's secret origin, and shakes up Miles' world in the process.
Leon's artwork focuses more on the emotional fallout, while DeLandro's is grittier and more noir influenced.
Valenza does a great job of establishing past and present with his color art.
Some truly painful moments that will make you feel for Miles.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Spawn '77 #2 delivers plenty of bloody action and a few genuinely striking visuals, especially when Spawn and the angel take center stage. Mark Spears handles the larger-than-life characters well, and the issue's final twist offers an intriguing reason to return. Unfortunately, the extra-sized page count doesn't feel entirely justified. With limited plot progression, extended action sequences, and…
pros: Excellent action choreography, particularly during the angel's brutal confrontation with police.
An intriguing cliffhanger introduces an unexpected twist.
cons: The nearly 60-page issue feels padded, with surprisingly little story progression.
Civilian character designs and flat backgrounds lack the visual polish of the supernatural characters.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Batman: Bad Seeds - Streets of Gotham #1 is a wonderfully human anthology that reminds us Gotham's greatest heroes don't always wear capes. Across six stories, an impressive lineup of creators explores how ordinary citizens respond when their city falls into chaos. The artwork is consistently strong, with each artist bringing a distinct personality to their corner of Gotham. It has plenty of heart…
pros: Six distinct stories offer compelling perspectives on everyday life during Gotham's latest crisis.
Excellent artwork throughout, particularly Jorge Fornes' gritty realism and Gretel Lusky's expressive character designs.
cons: Some stories are more memorable than others, with a few feeling relatively slight.
